what_this_is: The Workshop rows for tools/move-the-public-door: where the person's public door runs and the hosting and DNS rows it can move between, read from their Service connections list (record:service-connection); renting and releasing one host lease; and cutting one hostname over to a new address. Only the first reads that list, through the records door; the other three take the Service connections rows they need as input and answer their lease or cutover receipt, keeping nothing. Each reaches its held provider key through one credential mount; no key is printed or answered.

payload.label: See where the public door runs
payload.job: See where my public door runs now and which hosting services it can move between
payload.description: Takes the person's Service connections rows as `connections` (the caller reads them from the person's own store and hands them in) and answers where their public door runs now (its hosting row, its address and what proves it) and each hosting row with whether the door can move there and why not. It never reads or shows a key, reads no store and changes nothing.

connections.description: The record:service-connection rows as the person's own store holds them (each row's value: the kind, id, name, rents_a_host or hosting_provider fields). Read by the caller from its own store and handed in here; what is not given is not there.

payload.label: Rent a host for the public door
payload.job: Rent one server for my public door from my hosting service, or adopt a box I already run, and give me its lease
payload.description: Rents one server from the hosting row handed in as `hosting`, through that row's own requests only, and answers the lease: the provider, the server and SSH key identities, the address, size and place, and the cleanup deadline of a test host (within one day; a retained service has none). It keeps nothing: the person's AI stores the answered lease. Handed that same lease back as `lease`, it answers the lease it already holds. A server with the same name that this lease does not own is left untouched. When the provider's answer is lost, it removes only the server labelled with this lease's name. A row with no provider API (a box the person already runs) is adopted at the address given and is never deleted. The hosting key comes from the vault by the row's vault name and is never shown.

hosting.description: The value of the person's hosting row in the Service connections list (record:service-connection): the row whose rents_a_host block says how to ask the provider. The run mounts the key held under its rents_a_host.vault_key.

lease.description: The lease an earlier answer of this tool gave, handed back to be reused.

name.description: The server's name and the label that marks it as this lease's.

public_key.description: An ssh-ed25519 public key for the new server's administration.

address.description: The public IPv4 of a box the person already runs.

expires_at.description: UTC milliseconds a test host is removed by.

payload.label: Release a host of the public door
payload.job: Remove the server and SSH key one of my public door's host leases rented, and only those
payload.description: Removes the exact server and SSH key the lease handed in as `lease` names, through the requests of the hosting row it was rented from (handed in as `hosting`), after reading each one back and checking it still carries this lease's label, and answers the removed lease. It keeps nothing: the person's AI stores the answered lease. A server relabelled to someone else is left untouched. Handed a lease already removed, it answers the removed lease. A box the person already runs is only forgotten, never touched. The hosting key comes from the vault by the row's vault name and is never shown.

lease.description: The lease an earlier answer of rent-a-host-for-the-public-door gave.

hosting.description: The value of the hosting row the lease was rented from, in the Service connections list (record:service-connection). The run mounts the key held under its rents_a_host.vault_key.

payload.label: Cut a hostname over to a new address
payload.job: Point one exact hostname of mine at a new server's address, keeping every other DNS record and route, and roll it back if I ask
payload.description: Through the DNS provider description handed in as `dns` (the file the person keeps for it): `prepare` reads the zone and answers a `receipt` holding the one address record or managed binding that `hostname` holds now; `activate` points it at `address` and reads it back; `rollback` puts back what prepare read; `status` answers where the cutover stands without asking the provider; `keep-healthy` keeps `hostname` answering with exactly those of `candidates` (front-door computers, each `{ address, health_path? }`) that answer HTTP 200 on their health path, adding the healthy ones before it removes the others and refusing when none is healthy. `activate`, `rollback` and `status` take the `receipt` an earlier answer gave, and answer the changed receipt; the tool keeps nothing, so the person's AI stores it. Before every change it checks that no other record, guarded list or binding changed since prepare, and refuses when one did. A change whose answer was lost is reconciled from what the provider shows, never sent twice. The DNS key comes from the vault by the description's vault name and is never shown.

dns.description: The DNS provider description the person keeps: base, auth, vault_key, its requests and the zone, record and binding parts that say which request does what.

receipt.description: The receipt an earlier answer of this tool gave; required for activate, rollback and status.

address.description: prepare, activate and rollback: the new server's public IPv4.

candidates.description: keep-healthy: the front-door computers, each { address, health_path? }.

health_path.description: keep-healthy: the path asked of each computer when it names none (default /).

adopt.description: keep-healthy: take over the address records the name already holds.

payload.label: Step a hostname cut-over through the engine
payload.job: Work out the next DNS request that pointing one of my hostnames at a new address needs, at a DNS provider my engine reaches for me, so a workflow sends it
payload.description: For a DNS provider description reached through the engine (`transport: "engine"`, which holds no key): replays the cut-over named in `cutover` (prepare, activate, rollback or status, exactly as tool:cut-a-hostname-over-to-a-new-address does them) against the answers a workflow kept so far, `transcript` ([{ request: { name, arguments }, answer }] in the order asked, each answer as the engine's tools:run gave it), and answers `{ done: false, next: { name, arguments } }`, the next of the description's declared tools to ask with its arguments, or `{ done: true, answer }`, the cut-over's own answer with its receipt. It reaches nothing itself: every request goes out through the workflow's own ask step, which names its tool, so that step is the fence. Kept answers whose request is not the one the replay asks at that place refuse the step: they belong to another cut-over, and the run starts again.

dns.description: The DNS provider description the person keeps, with transport "engine": base, its requests (each naming one tool of the provider's server) and the zone and record parts that say which request does what.

receipt.description: The receipt an earlier cut-over's answer gave; required for activate, rollback and status.

address.description: prepare, activate and rollback: the new server's public IPv4.

transcript.description: Every request this cut-over asked so far with the engine's answer, in order; [] for the first step.
